# Technical document: ball possession (More than a Hack 2027, Phase 1)

**Team:** DeculGirl
**Repository:** https://github.com/DyangPB/mtah-DeculGirl-submission
**Submitted file:** `DeculGirl.csv`, generated by `python tools/make_own.py` (it writes `results/DeculGirl_own.csv`; the
upload is a copy renamed after the team). SHA-256 of the submitted file, LF line endings:
`10ef2d3626d39f910d35820057c7d45e47879faeba0d8ff0a0635b3abe30c480`
**Environment:** Python 3.10.7, numpy 1.26.4, pandas 2.2.2 (pinned in `requirements.txt`)

## 1. Summary

A rule-based pipeline with no learned model and no training. It labels every video frame of the tactical
recording `H`, `A`, `D` or `X` using **only the automatic tracking** (ATD). Possession is a state that persists:
a team gets the ball on evidence, and keeps it until evidence from the other team or a dead ball. Dead ball is
decided by five independent layers. Every parameter is a stated football or physics assumption, not a value
optimised against the match, its public ground truth or its video. The public ground truth did inform the layers
and the order of magnitude of the speed thresholds; section 7 says exactly how.

It is **not proven to be more accurate than the organisers' baseline** on the full match. What is shown, and what
is not, is in sections 7 and 8.

## 2. Approach

1. **Candidate team per frame.** On a frame with a tracked ball, a team is a candidate if its nearest player is
   within 2.0 m of the ball and closer than the other team's nearest player by more than 1.0 m. A candidacy
   must last 5 frames in a row (0.2 s) to count, so fleeting touches are ignored.
2. **Persistence.** The label stays with the current team (no time limit) until the other team has accumulated
   10 frames of candidacy (0.4 s; evidence separated by more than 25 frames does not add up). A confirmed
   switch is dated back to the first frame of its evidence, so confirmation adds no delay.
3. **Gaps without a ball.** The ball is untracked on about 41% of graded frames. There the last team keeps the
   ball. If a switch is confirmed right after such a gap, the gap is split at its midpoint between the old and
   the new team (the weakest guess in the pipeline, kept as the documented default).
4. **Dead ball (`D`)**, any of five layers, restricted to graded frames, with gaps under 1 s bridged and runs
   shorter than 2 s dropped:
   - ball outside the pitch for at least 1 s;
   - ball inside a 1 m circle for 1 s **and** the median player speed under 1.0 m/s;
   - the median player speed under 0.5 m/s for 10 s, ball seen or not (long stoppages);
   - players clustered (RMS distance from their centroid under 16 m) **and** slower than 1.0 m/s for 5 s;
   - frames 110,808-113,741: graded, and all `D`, as published in the organisers' FAQ.
5. **Assembly.** Possession is computed separately inside each stretch of live play, so it never carries across a
   stoppage; the first team to be confirmed after a restart owns the frames before it (look-ahead, since
   processing is offline). Frames outside the two graded ranges are `X`.

Result on the 158,857 graded frames: 74,550 `H` (46.9%), 65,359 `A` (41.1%), 18,948 `D` (11.9%), about 200 label
runs per half, 341 possessions.

## 3. Assets

- **Used:** tactical tracking (ATD): positions of the track slots and of the ball, and the team of each slot.
  Player speed is **recomputed** from positions (displacement over 1 s, jumps above 12 m/s discarded); it matches
  the file's own speed column (median ratio 0.95).
- **Examined and dropped:**
  - The ball-speed column of the ATD. It is present in only 1.2% of detected-ball frames in the graded halves,
    so ball speed is not used; the "still ball" layer uses position instead.
  - A first version of the dead-ball thresholds (quiet team under 1.0 m/s, ball-still layer under 1.5 m/s). It
    labelled 27.7% of graded frames as `D`. The cause was the assumption: the median speed of all tracked players
    is ~1.35 m/s through the graded halves, so 28% of graded frames are already below 1.0 m/s. The thresholds were
    lowered to 0.5 and 1.0 m/s using that statistic of the tracking.
  - A `huddle` layer adds only 0.5% of graded frames and changes nothing on the public window. Kept, because
    it has a stated reason and is cheap.
- **Not used:** the video, the broadcast recording, the homography, Smart Tagging.

## 4. Training data

None. No labelled dataset was used and nothing was trained or optimised on the provided game, its ground
truth or its video.

## 5. Possession rules implemented

- A team has the ball when its nearest player is within 2 m and clearly closer than the other team's, and holds
  that for 5 frames. A pass that only goes close to a player is not a change; a switch needs 10 frames of evidence.
- Loose, contested or untracked ball: possession stays with the last team (no time limit).
- Restart: ownership does not carry across a stoppage. The first team confirmed after the restart owns it.
- Dead ball: out of the pitch, still ball with slow players, a standing team, a clustered slow team, and the
  published pre-kick-off block of the second half. Dead-ball ownership is not asked for, so `D` carries no team.
- Aerial duels cannot be recognised (the coordinates have no height); the pipeline only refuses to switch too fast.
- Minimum possession length: nothing is merged or dropped, because the shortest real possession in the public
  ground truth is 19 frames and the scorer does not merge short ones.

## 6. Parameters and where they come from

| Parameter | Value | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Control distance / margin | 2.0 m / 1.0 m | Reach of a player controlling the ball; tracking error is about 1 m |
| Candidacy / switch evidence | 5 / 10 frames | Filters fleeting touches; must stay below 19 frames, the shortest real possession |
| Evidence gap | 25 frames | A brief tracking drop-out should not reset the count |
| Out of pitch | 1 s | One full second is not a tracking flicker |
| Ball still | 1 m over 1 s, i.e. under 1 m/s | The "still ball" figure of the possession rules |
| Slow players (with ball still / clustered) | median under 1.0 m/s | Median of all tracked players is ~1.35 m/s in play |
| Standing team | median under 0.5 m/s for 10 s | Under 0.5 m/s is about 9% of graded frames; long enough to be a stoppage |
| Clustered | RMS spread under 16 m for 5 s | Median spread is ~21 m in open play; under 16 m is the bottom ~4% |
| Shortest dead run / bridge | 2 s / 1 s | A throw-in lasts 5-8 s; shorter drop-outs are not a restart |
| Speed estimate | displacement over 1 s, 12 m/s jump limit | Reduces noise; faster than a sprint is a tracking jump |
| Pre-kick-off block | frames 110,808-113,741 | Published in the organisers' FAQ |

Transparency note: the signals of the layers were first read from the four dead-ball blocks of the public ground
truth (descriptive statistics, section 7), and the first thresholds were revised after seeing that the share of
`D` was too large. Thresholds were not fitted to those blocks.

## 7. Use of the public ground truth

The 5-minute public file was used several times: to check that the pipeline runs end to end, to read how the
tracking behaves in its four dead-ball blocks, and to score each version of the pipeline and read its per-class
precision and recall. What the blocks showed: ball detected 66% of the time in `D` against 100% / 85% in `H` / `A`;
median player speed 1.19 m/s in `D` against 2.05 / 2.47 (taken from the speed column of the tracking file, not from
our own estimate); nearest player to the ball 2.9 m against 1.6 / 1.7.

That reading informed the layers and the order of magnitude of the speed thresholds, which were set below the
speeds seen in those blocks. The thresholds were not optimised against the ground truth or its score, and the one
revision made (the first quiet-team threshold, section 3) was triggered by the share of `D` looking too large
(27.7% of graded frames, against about 20% in the public window), then justified from the distribution of the
tracking itself. No version was selected from its score, and the dead-ball recall problem it exposed (0.07) was
left as it is rather than fixed by fitting the four blocks.

Public check (17 possessions, too few to rank on): spellF1 **0.3758**, macroF1 0.5600 (`D` precision 0.98, recall
0.07). The baseline scores 0.3256 and 0.6207 on the same window. The scorer's own bootstrap states that gaps below
about 0.33 are inside the noise, so this gap is not evidence.

Checks that do not need the answer key, over both graded halves:

| | `baseline_smooth50` | this pipeline |
|---|---|---|
| `H`/`A` possessions | 594 | 341 |
| Possessions shorter than 19 frames | 98 | 4 |
| Median possession length | 4.6 s | 10.0 s |

It differs from `baseline_smooth50` on 66,949 of the 158,857 graded frames (42.1%). Its team labels agree 86.6%
with an independently built pipeline from a teammate (not submitted), on the 129,076 graded frames where both say
`H` or `A`; 72% of its `D` frames are also `D` there.

## 8. Limitations

- **Dead-ball recall is weak.** On the public window `D` precision is 0.98 but recall is 0.07: when it says dead
  ball it is almost always right, but it finds few of the dead balls. Two of the four public blocks have the ball
  tracked and players moving at normal speed; no tracking-only rule found here separates them without being tuned
  to those blocks, which was not done.
- **Long missing-ball stretches.** The ball is untracked on about 41% of graded frames, often for tens of seconds.
  There the pipeline only holds the last team and has no model of play from the players alone.
- **The midpoint guess** for a switch hidden inside a gap is arbitrary.
- **Thresholds are unverified** on external data and rest on assumptions about speed and distance.
- **Frozen tracker versus real stoppage** cannot be told apart without the video.
- **Accuracy on the full match is not demonstrated.** No answer key exists outside the public 5 minutes.

## 9. With more time

Use the Smart Tagging set-piece windows to place dead balls (a teammate's independent pipeline does, and labels
more dead-ball frames than this one); model the missing-ball periods from team shape and movement; replace the
hold-last rule and the midpoint guess by a decoder with an explicit switching cost; verify the thresholds on an
external dataset with tracking and events, licence permitting.

## 10. Reproduction

The pipeline is deterministic: no randomness is used.

```bash
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1          # Windows PowerShell
pip install -r requirements.txt
python tools/fetch_official.py      # official scorer and validator, pinned
# unpack the data bundle into ./data (or set MTAH_DATA_DIR)
python tools/make_own.py            # writes results/DeculGirl_own.csv
python third_party/mtah2027/evaluation/validate_submission.py results/DeculGirl_own.csv
```

The first run parses the tracking file (about 25 s) and caches it in `data/cache_tracking.npz`. Rebuilding after
deleting the cache gave a byte-identical file (MD5 `b9aca403d7b956b170a403497a259ff3` both times). The SHA-256 in
the header is for the copy uploaded as `DeculGirl.csv`; it is the same content, so on Windows or Linux the labels
are identical and only the line endings may differ if the file is re-saved elsewhere.
